problem: KDP 70% royalty only applies within a price band ($2.99-$12.99 on Amazon.com since 2026-07-07) and deducts a per-MB delivery fee; outside it authors get 35%.
saga_solution: Flat author share at any price, no delivery fee; show exact payout before publishing

problem: KDP pays about 60 days after month end (90 for expanded distribution), creating cash-flow lag.

sources.title: KDP: when will I get paid

workarounds: Direct sales via Stripe/Payhip for faster payouts
saga_solution: Weekly payouts after a refund window via Stripe Connect

problem: Kindle+ (formerly Kindle Unlimited) pays from a discretionary monthly pool per KENP page; per-page rate is not known in advance and requires KDP Select exclusivity.

sources.title: Written Word Media: Kindle+ for authors

saga_solution: Non-exclusive subscription with published, fixed payout formula

problem: Exclusivity (KDP Select) is required for 70% in Brazil, Japan, Mexico, India and for Kindle+ income, locking authors out of other stores.
workarounds: Rotate titles in/out of Select in 90-day terms
saga_solution: Never require exclusivity

problem: Authors get no buyer emails from retailers, so the reader relationship belongs to the store.

sources.title: Written Word Media 2026 mid-year indie author survey

workarounds: Reader magnets via BookFunnel, newsletters, back-matter links
saga_solution: Opt-in, reader-controlled sharing of contact with the author at purchase

problem: Discoverability increasingly requires paid ads (Amazon Ads usage rises to 59% in the 'got traction' tier) and AI-generated content floods the market.

sources.title: Written Word Media 2026 mid-year indie author survey

saga_solution: Club/community-driven discovery and bookstore curation rather than pay-to-rank

problem: Going wide via Draft2Digital now costs a $20 activation fee (new accounts) and $12/yr for low earners, plus ~10% of retail.
saga_solution: Free listing on SAGA; distribution-to-others as optional paid service

problem: Direct-sales stacks need several tools (store, payment, delivery app, tax); each charges fees (Payhip 5% free plan, Gumroad 10%+50c, BookFunnel $30-$300/yr).
saga_solution: All-in-one author storefront with delivery to any app and tax handled

problem: Lemon Squeezy is closed to new sign-ups and shutting down 2027-03-31, stranding creators who chose it as merchant of record.
saga_solution: Stable MoR-backed checkout with exportable customer lists

problem: AI-generated content must be disclosed on KDP; AI-assisted need not be, leaving readers unable to distinguish and honest authors competing with floods.

sources.title: Written Word Media 2026 mid-year indie author survey

saga_solution: Visible AI-disclosure labels and provenance metadata in SAGA store

problem: Piracy fear drives DRM use, but DRM restricts legitimate readers; Amazon now lets DRM-free KDP books be downloaded as EPUB/PDF since 2026-01-20.
saga_solution: Default watermarking (social DRM) with author-selectable LCP

problem: Sales reporting is fragmented across stores with different delays and formats.

sources.title: KDP: when will I get paid

saga_solution: Real-time sales dashboard; import other stores' reports

problem: Retailers are dropping ONIX 2.1; Amazon stopped accepting it end of March 2026, forcing ONIX 3.0/3.1 migrations.

sources.title: BookNet Canada: Amazon ends ONIX 2.1 March 2026

saga_solution: Accept ONIX 3.x ingest from day one; also simple web form for small presses

problem: ISBNs cost $125 single / $295 for 10 / $575 for 100 from Bowker in the US.
saga_solution: Do not require ISBN for SAGA-only listings; support ISBN when present

problem: European Accessibility Act applies to ebooks made available from 2025-06-28: accessible EPUB, accessibility metadata (ONIX list 196), accessibility statement.

sources.title: BookNet Canada: Amazon ends ONIX 2.1 March 2026

saga_solution: Built-in accessibility checker at upload and accessible reading system

problem: DRM options: Adobe ACS is legacy; Readium LCP is an ISO standard (ISO/IEC 23078-2:2024) with yearly certification fee and no per-transaction cost.
saga_solution: Support LCP for publishers who require it; watermarking default

problem: Big-five and most trade catalog cannot be sold without distribution contracts, agency pricing terms and approved DRM.

sources.title: Publishers Weekly: Bookshop.org debuts e-book platform

saga_solution: Start with indie/small-press and public-domain catalog; pursue distributor deals later

problem: Reporting pain: payment and sales reports arrive monthly with long lag; library reports differ again.

sources.title: KDP: when will I get paid

saga_solution: Per-title daily reports and API export

problem: Bookshop.org (launched ebooks 2025-01-28) gives stores 30% of sale on affiliate purchases and 10% pool for unattributed sales; but iOS rules forced web-only purchase.

sources.title: Publishers Weekly: Bookshop.org debuts e-book platform

saga_solution: Partner rather than compete: let stores curate shelves and earn affiliate share in SAGA

problem: Bookshop.org ebooks cannot be read on Kindle and indie self-published titles were not available at launch.

sources.title: Publishers Weekly: Bookshop.org debuts e-book platform

saga_solution: Indie-author catalog plus DRM-free EPUB export to any reader

problem: Previous indie ebook partners churned: ABA's Hummingbird integration ended 2022-09-30 after an acquisition; Kobo partnership (from 2012) preceded it.

sources.title: ABA: Hummingbird no longer on IndieCommerce

saga_solution: Durable data portability guarantees for stores (customer lists, libraries survive SAGA changes)

problem: Libro.fm proves stores will promote a digital partner that shares revenue, but its exact share is not public on its site.
saga_solution: Transparent published store share

problem: Instructors pay or pass on per-student fees for social annotation (Perusall $5-$25 per student, institutional licenses).
saga_solution: Free annotation on owned books; institutional plan for LMS integration

problem: Automatic textbook billing ('inclusive access') criticised for opt-out billing and access that expires.

sources.title: CARL statement on automatic textbook billing

saga_solution: Owned, non-expiring files and OER-friendly pricing; avoid auto-billing models

problem: Reading analytics in courseware raise FERPA/privacy concerns; rights transfer to students at 18/postsecondary.
saga_solution: Aggregate-only, opt-in analytics; no per-student reading surveillance sold to third parties

problem: Annotations are locked in proprietary formats; W3C Web Annotation Data Model (Recommendation, 2017) exists but few readers export it.
saga_solution: Store and export highlights as W3C annotations plus BibTeX/RIS/CSL-JSON citations

problem: Ebooks bought on most platforms are licenses tied to one app; portability is limited.
saga_solution: DRM-free-by-default library with EPUB download and reader-owned backups

problem: Library ebooks have long holds because libraries pay ~$55+ for 2-year single-user licenses vs ~$13 consumer price.

sources.title: Urban Libraries Council: E-Book Pricing Crisis 2026

saga_solution: Do not compete with libraries; offer indie titles to libraries on fair perpetual/metered terms later

problem: Amazon dominates US ebooks (Amazon-claimed 67% of US digital book sales; estimate, not audited).

sources.title: Good e-Reader: Amazon dominant in ebook sales (claimed 67%)

saga_solution: Niche positioning (ownership, clubs, indie) rather than head-on competition

problem: US ebook market is small and flat: AAP reports $2.2B ebook revenue in 2025 (+3.2%).
saga_solution: Revenue beyond book sales (tools, hardware, institutional)

problem: iOS in-app purchases cost up to 30%; since the 2025-04-30 Epic order US apps may link out (Kindle added 'Get Book'), but the Ninth Circuit (2025-12-11) allows Apple a yet-to-be-set commission.

sources.title: MacRumors: Kindle app Get Book button (May 2025)
MacRumors: Ninth Circuit modifies Epic injunction (Dec 2025)

saga_solution: Web checkout with US external link; budget for a future Apple link fee

problem: Fixed card fees make cheap ebooks expensive to process: Stripe 2.9%+30c is ~8.9% of a $4.99 sale; MoR 5%+50c is ~15%.
saga_solution: Prepaid wallet / cart batching; keep take >= 15% at low price points

problem: Tax compliance: EU VAT is charged at buyer's country rate on ebooks; UK ebooks zero-rated since 2020-05-01.
saga_solution: MoR early, Stripe Tax later once volume justifies

problem: Google Play pays 70% in 60+ countries regardless of price after accepting new ToS; Apple pays 70% regardless of price with no delivery fee, undercutting KDP's band rules.

sources.title: Google Play Books revenue split FAQ

saga_solution: Match the 'any price, no delivery fee' norm
